mission: Ben bypasses the Jedi partner roster and calls Desh Rolan. The choice looks pragmatic and is; it is also the third solo move of the evening.
why_now: The mission needs a second body before departure. Ben has the comm in his hand and the roster one tap away. The decision happens quickly enough that it could be reflex — which is the problem.
conflict: Ben tells himself Desh is the right call — quiet, deniable, experienced. The Knight on the roster would be a better fit on paper. Ben does not open the roster.
turning_point: Desh answers the comm with dry humor and agrees to the job without asking why Ben did not call a Jedi. They both know why, and neither says so.
opening_hook: Ben sits in his ship's cockpit with the preflight complete and his thumb sliding past the Jedi partner roster to open his personal contacts instead
closing_hook: The wrongness in the Force shifts as Ben leaves Coruscant — not diminishing but acquiring direction, like a compass needle settling
emotional_trajectory: Calculated avoidance -> familiar comfort with Desh -> unsettled recognition that the wrongness is guiding him

stakes.personal: Ben's self-deception about why he chooses isolation over Jedi partnership
stakes.interpersonal: The Ben/Desh dynamic — friendship built on shared history neither discusses
stakes.external: The wrongness has a direction — it is pulling Ben somewhere specific

setting: Jedi Temple hangar bay -> comm call to Desh -> departure from Coruscant
sensory_details: Hangar echoes and service-tech chatter in the background; Desh's voice tinny over long-range comm, warm under the static; hyperspace entry — the wrongness persists through the jump, which it should not
canon_elements_needed: Galactic Alliance Guard history, dissolution, and legacy
Non-Force-sensitive relationships with Jedi in post-war era
Coruscant to Outer Rim hyperspace travel routes and duration
Jedi Temple hangar bay layout and departure protocols
action_beats: Ben bypasses three Jedi Knight contacts on his datapad and opens his personal list
Desh's voice crackles over long-range comm — dry greeting, no questions asked
Ben's ship lifts from the Temple hangar bay and angles toward orbit
The ship punches into hyperspace; Ben's instruments flicker as the wrongness persists through the jump
promises_planted: Ben and Desh share unspoken GAG history (PP02)
Desh will matter to the climax (PP19)
notes: R01 lands at the close of the scene — the wrongness acquires direction during hyperspace transit, which it should not. This is the chapter's turn: the disturbance stops being ambient and starts being a compass. Relationship turn: Ben/Desh from dormant contact to operational partnership — Desh takes the job without asking for the rationale Ben cannot give. GAG onboarding — two beats and no more: that Ben served in it as a teenager, and that it is the thing he and Desh share. Handle this in Zahn-style integration — a concise phrase or two threaded through Ben's reaction when he registers Desh's unspoken understanding, not a standalone exposition paragraph. The information rides on top of a beat (Ben's physical action, Desh's tone, a specific memory) rather than pausing the scene as narrator commentary. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, articulate a 'self-reliance is safety' frame. The choice is behavioural. If his interiority reaches for a thesis sentence about Jacen, Vestara, or trust, cut it; the scene earns its weight through what he does, not what he says about what he does. Desh's arc starts here: he arrives as a favor, obligation not yet purpose.
